title: Install Docker Engine & Compose in WSL2

user_story.i_want: Docker Engine and Docker Compose v2 running inside my WSL2 distro
user_story.so_that: I can run the free AWS stand-ins locally

description: Docker is not installed in the WSL distro yet (checked 2026-11-16: `docker: command not found`). Recommended: install Docker Engine from Docker's own apt repository *inside* WSL. It's free with no licence terms, and the daemon runs via systemd. Alternative: Docker Desktop on Windows with WSL integration enabled. Its licence is free for personal use; check the terms if you use it at work. You run every command yourself; Claude only explains.

acceptance_criteria.then: both the Client and Server sections print, without sudo

acceptance_criteria.given: WSL was fully restarted (`wsl --shutdown` from Windows, then reopen)
acceptance_criteria.then: the daemon is reachable without starting it by hand

technical_notes: Remove conflicting packages first (docker.io, podman-docker, etc.), as Docker's Ubuntu guide lists.
Make sure `/etc/wsl.conf` contains `[boot]` with `systemd=true` so the Docker service starts with WSL.
Do the Linux post-install step (add your user to the `docker` group), then open a new shell.
